title: transcript replay and live batches
asserts: subscribing is answered at once with the history the core kept as one replay frame, every record read afterwards arrives as a live batch whose seq numbers are strictly above the replayed ones, so a client that appends by seq and drops a seq it already holds loses nothing and duplicates nothing, and no batch is pushed after unsubscribe.

steps.note: the fake agent writes this turn into claude's own jsonl, which is the plane's source; the pty bytes it also prints are a different plane and are ignored here
long enough for the core to have read the turn BEFORE anyone subscribes, so what comes back is history rather than a live batch that happened to be in flight
one turn is three records - the prompt that opened it, the model request, and the prose - and the replay carries all of them, not the tail of one
append, never replace: every seq in a live batch is above every seq the replay carried, which is what makes dedup-by-seq a client's whole job
the records are still read - this connection just stopped being told, the same way unsubscribeQueue works
